subject: [RFC PATCH 1/5] mm: let folio_mkclean() report which pages had dirty PTEs

2026-09-03.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new function, folio_mkclean_dirtymap(), which reports the pages of a folio that had dirty PTEs during the clearing process. The existing folio_mkclean() function is modified to use this new function and pass no bitmap, maintaining its original behavior. This change allows for more accurate tracking of page modifications in large folios, where only the per-entry dirty bit was previously recorded.

reviews.author: Usama Arif
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that holding the page-table lock prevents another kernel thread from changing the PTE, but does not prevent the CPU from setting the hardware dirty bit, leading to a timing window where the bitmap is populated from an outdated snapshot of the PTEs. This issue arises in range-aware iomap writeback scenarios and can result in incorrect final dirty state.
reviews.raw_body:
The patch reads the PTE first and then records pte_dirty(entry) in the bitmap
before invalidating the PTE.

Holding the page-table lock prevents another kernel thread from changing
the PTE, but it does not prevent the CPU from setting the hardware dirty
bit.

This sequence is possible:

  Writeback CPU                  Application CPU
  -------------                  ---------------
  ptep_get(): writable, clean
                                 store through the PTE
                                 hardware sets dirty
  ptep_clear_flush(): returns dirty PTE
  pte_mkclean()
  reinstall clean, read-only PTE

The bitmap was populated from the first, clean snapshot. The dirty state
returned by ptep_clear_flush() is discarded.

With range-aware iomap writeback:

- The folio can still be selected for writeback.
- The affected filesystem block is absent from the iomap dirty bitmap.
- Writeback clears the folio dirty state without writing that block.
- Later eviction can discard the modified data.

The old whole-folio behavior did not need to know which PTE became
dirty, so this timing window was harmless. Sub-folio tracking makes the
final dirty state correctness-critical.

The PMD path has the identical race between pmdp_get() and
pmdp_invalidate().

2026-09-09.patch_summary: This patch modifies the folio_mkclean() function to report which pages had dirty PTEs by introducing a new function, folio_mkclean_dirtymap(). The latter takes a bitmap and sets a bit for every page of the folio whose entry was dirty. The original folio_mkclean() function is now a wrapper that passes no bitmap, preserving its existing behavior. This change allows downstream code to track which parts of a large folio were written through a mapping, rather than assuming the whole folio changed.
